# MatchGraph { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph(
    claims=None,
    *,
    units=None,
    axis=None,
    source=None,
    source_id=None,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
```

A graph of MatchClaims connecting events across timelines/groups.

The MatchGraph builds a networkx graph where:
- Nodes: (timeline_id, coordinate) tuples
- Edges: synchronous AlignmentAnchors, stated by a MatchClaim or
  inferred through a group (:class:`InferredEdge`)

Only synchronous claims produce graph edges. Non-synchronous claims
(conceptual matches, NOMATCH) are stored in ``_claims`` but do not
create nodes or edges. The graph's MatchClaims are those it was given;
what it infers is held apart, in :attr:`inferred_edges`.

Each Hendrix M-box (M1–M15) is a separate MatchGraph. The system
is NOT a global graph; MatchGraphs are created on demand.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name           | Type                                                                         | Description                                                      |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| claims         | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\]    | The MatchClaims of this graph (synchronous and non-synchronous). |
| inferred_edges | [list](`list`)\[[InferredEdge](`timetoalign.alignment.graph.InferredEdge`)\] | The edges the graph inferred through groups.                     |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Build a graph from two claims between notes of a score and onsets
of a recording:

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline, TimelineGroup
>>> def claim(quarters, seconds):
...     return MatchClaim(
...         timeline_a_id="score",
...         timeline_b_id="audio",
...         event_a_id=f"note_{quarters}",
...         event_b_id=f"onset_{quarters}",
...         start_anchor=AlignmentAnchor(
...             timeline_a_id="score",
...             coordinate_a=Coordinate(quarters, TimeUnit.quarters),
...             timeline_b_id="audio",
...             coordinate_b=Coordinate(seconds, TimeUnit.seconds),
...         ),
...         is_synchronous=True,
...     )
>>> graph = MatchGraph(claims=[claim(0, 0.0), claim(4, 2.0)])
>>> graph.n_nodes, graph.n_edges, graph.n_components
(4, 2, 2)
```

Extend it through the group the score shares with its parts:

```python
>>> score = Timeline(length=8, unit=TimeUnit.quarters, uid="score")
>>> parts = Timeline(length=8, unit=TimeUnit.quarters, uid="parts")
>>> group = TimelineGroup(name="edition", timelines=[score, parts])
>>> extended = graph.extend_to_groups({group.id: group})
>>> extended.n_nodes, extended.n_edges, extended.n_claims
(6, 4, 2)
>>> extended.inferred_edges[0].group_id == group.id
True
>>> extended.inferred_edges[0].source_claim.event_a_id
'note_0'
```

One stamp per synchronized position:

```python
>>> stamps = extended.get_stamps()
>>> print(stamps[1])
MatchStamp (3 timelines, 2 edges)
  audio   2 seconds  stated
  parts  4 quarters  inferred
  score  4 quarters  stated
```

### extend_to_groups { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.extend_to_groups }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.extend_to_groups(
    groups,
    *,
    include_inferred=True,
    within=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
```

Extend anchors to full group timestamps via inferred edges.

For each coordinate in the graph, computes the equivalent coordinate
for every other member of every group its timeline belongs to and
adds an edge between the two, recorded as an :class:`InferredEdge`
(the anchor, the group, and the MatchClaim the coordinate traces
back to) in the extended graph's :attr:`inferred_edges`. The
extended graph holds the same MatchClaims as this one: an inferred
edge is the graph's own, never a MatchClaim. Membership is read from
*groups* alone, and a timeline may belong to several. A coordinate
reached this way is extended in turn through the other groups of its
timeline, so a timeline shared by two groups carries a coordinate
from the members of one to the members of the other. Filters control
which timelines receive inferred edges; a timeline they exclude
receives no coordinate, so no extension passes through it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                                  | Description                                | Default    |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|------------|
| groups           | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), \'TimelineGroup\'\]                     | Dict of group_id -> TimelineGroup.         | _required_ |
| include_inferred | [bool](`bool`)                                                        | Whether to add inferred edges.             | `True`     |
| within           | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                  | Only extend to these timeline IDs.         | `None`     |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Regex filter for timeline IDs.             | `None`     |
| include_domains  | [set](`set`)\[[Domain](`timetoalign.core.enums.Domain`)\] \| None     | Only extend to timelines in these domains. | `None`     |
| include_units    | [set](`set`)\[[TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.enums.TimeUnit`)\] \| None | Only extend to timelines with these units. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                                    |
|--------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchGraph\' | New MatchGraph with extended edges (or self if not extending). |

### filter { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.filter }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.filter(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    within=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    stated_only=False,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
```

Return the graph of the MatchClaims the filters keep.

The filters choose claims, with the meaning they have on every
MatchClaim query (:meth:`~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_match_claims`),
decided by :meth:`~timetoalign.alignment.filters.ClaimFilter.select`.
The result is the graph of the kept claims: a graph extended through
groups (:meth:`extend_to_groups`) is extended again through the same
groups, under the same filters, and reaches only the timelines
``within``, ``include_domains`` and ``include_units`` admit. So it
holds exactly what a graph built from the kept claims and extended
the same way holds.

Domains and units are read from the source bundle's timelines when
the graph has a source, else from the units of the graph's anchors
and of the graph it was filtered from (a filtered graph keeps the
units its own source graph knew, so filters compose in any order):
without a source, a claim on a timeline no anchor names (a NOMATCH
or conceptual claim, say) passes no domain or unit filter.

The groups are read as they stand when filtering: a member added to
a group after the extension is reached by the filtered graph.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                       | Default           |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| timeline_id      | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Only the claims with this timeline on either side; a timeline the graph does not know gives no claim.                                                             | `None`            |
| timeline_ids     | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                   | Only the claims with any of these timelines on either side.                                                                                                       | `None`            |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | Only the claims with a timeline whose ID the regex finds (``re.search``) on either side.                                                                          | `None`            |
| within           | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                   | Only the claims whose both timelines are in this set; the extension reaches only these timelines.                                                                 | `None`            |
| synchronous_only | [bool](`bool`)                                                                         | Only the synchronous claims (conceptual and NOMATCH claims excluded).                                                                                             | `False`           |
| nomatch_only     | [bool](`bool`)                                                                         | Only the NOMATCH claims (an event on one side, the sentinel on the other); they hold no anchor, so the result has no edge.                                        | `False`           |
| stated_only      | [bool](`bool`)                                                                         | Only the edges MatchClaims state: the result is not extended through groups.                                                                                      | `False`           |
| include_domains  | [set](`set`)\[[Domain](`timetoalign.core.enums.Domain`)\] \| None                      | Only the claims whose both timelines are in these domains; the extension reaches only these domains.                                                              | `None`            |
| include_units    | [set](`set`)\[[TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.enums.TimeUnit`)\] \| None                  | Only the claims whose both timelines have these units; the extension reaches only these units.                                                                    | `None`            |
| believer         | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                   | The actor whose beliefs filter the claims (the belief filter, actors compared as IRIs under the source bundle's manifest ``@context``); ``None`` filters nothing. | `None`            |
| beliefs          | [Collection](`collections.abc.Collection`)\[[BeliefState](`timetoshare.BeliefState`)\] | The states kept for the believer (``"true"``, ``"undecided"``, ``"unlikely"``, ``"false"``); default all but ``"false"``.                                         | `DEFAULT_BELIEFS` |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                          |
|--------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchGraph\' | A new MatchGraph of the kept claims. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                     |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If ``synchronous_only`` and ``nomatch_only`` are both set, or ``beliefs`` is not a collection of belief states. |

### get_matchstamp { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.get_matchstamp }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.get_matchstamp()
```

Get the single MatchStamp for this graph.

One MatchGraph = one MatchStamp. The MatchStamp is the union of
all coordinates reachable through the graph's edges.

If the graph contains multiple disconnected components, this
method raises ``ValueError`` -- each component should be its own
MatchGraph. Use ``split_components()`` to separate them first, or
use the multi-component ``get_stamps()`` method.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                            |
|--------|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchStamp\' | Single MatchStamp spanning all timelines in the graph. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the graph has multiple disconnected components. |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the graph has no synchronous claims (no nodes). |

#### See Also {.doc-section .doc-section-see-also}

`split_components`: Split a multi-component graph into separate
    MatchGraph objects.
`get_stamps`: Multi-component method returning one stamp per component.

### get_stamps { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.get_stamps }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.get_stamps()
```

Get all MatchStamps from the graph.

Returns one MatchStamp per connected component, each containing
all coordinates reachable from that component.

Returns:
    List of MatchStamps, one per connected component.

### split_components { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.split_components }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.split_components()
```

Split this graph into one MatchGraph per connected component.

Each returned MatchGraph represents a single connected component
and can be queried with ``get_matchstamp()``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                             | Description                                              |
|--------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[\'MatchGraph\'\] | List of MatchGraph objects, one per connected component. |
|        | [list](`list`)\[\'MatchGraph\'\] | Empty list if the graph has no synchronous claims.       |

### to_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchGraph.to_dict }

```python
alignment.MatchGraph.to_dict()
```

Serialize to dictionary.

Note: This serializes the claims, not the full graph.
The graph can be rebuilt from claims; its inferred edges are not
written, and extending the rebuilt graph through the same groups
infers them again.
